Author: EM-FREE-333687 / TASK_RESEARCH
Activity: RA-4B9056969903914852506E59 (the existing TASK activity; no new formal Task/claim).

Result: NOT_APPLICABLE_DIRECT_HYODO_KATO_5_1; narrower relative interfaces located, LC still OPEN.

## Exact target

The fixed geometry paper requires LC for a proper semistable genus-one family over Spf Z_p[[t]], with the log divisor t=0, theta(t)=t^p and coefficient Frobenius identity on the Z_p descent. It needs:
A. the correct relative log-crystalline/log-de Rham realization over this formal base and passage to Q_p[[t]];
B. the generic horizontal identification with the actual source H^1;
C. regular Frobenius isogeny for theta with geometric generic restriction and cup multiplier p;
D. normalization-compatible specialization identifying graph H^1 with the residue-kernel line and its actual split-branch Frobenius action.

These are the LC A-D interface of my fixed nonauthor review. I am now the applicability researcher for that previously reviewed gap. This new source investigation is not independent review of its own eventual import.

## Primary source actually retrieved and read

Osamu Hyodo and Kazuya Kato, “Semi-stable reduction and crystalline cohomology with logarithmic poles”, Astérisque 223 (1994), Exposé V, pp. 221–268.

Official landing page:
https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1994__223__221_0/

Official PDF:
https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1994__223__221_0.pdf

The complete retrieved PDF has 49 pages including the cover, 1,867,725 bytes, SHA256 220873e91f89094d14f1a82631c6887a40ec362139990928236ca0525b1050cf. Its linearized length and final EOF match. It was converted with pdftotext; the decisive printed page 262 (PDF page 43) was also rendered and visually inspected. This is actual primary-text evidence, not a citation reconstructed from memory.

One mathematical primary source was inspected. Search-engine pages and a Crossref hit for a different 2021 “II” paper did not supply any mathematical premise. No second/third theorem source was opened.

## A decisive direct-import mismatch

Theorem 5.1, printed pp. 262–263, requires A to be a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field K of characteristic zero and a **perfect residue field k of characteristic p>0**. It concerns proper log-smooth X over that DVR, with Cartier-type reduction, and compares a special-fiber log-crystalline object with generic-fiber de Rham cohomology.

The exact target's coefficient ring is A=Z_p[[t]], with independent p and t parameters. It is a two-dimensional regular local ring, not a DVR: its maximal ideal (p,t) is not principal. Thus Theorem 5.1's actual base hypothesis fails. A proof that the elliptic fiber is an ordinary split node does not repair this base mismatch.

Two tempting one-dimensional replacements also fail the displayed hypotheses:
1. A=Q_p[[t]] is a complete DVR with uniformizer t, but its residue field is Q_p of characteristic zero, not characteristic p.
2. The p-adic completion of Z_p[[t]] localized at the height-one prime (p) is a mixed-characteristic DVR with residue field F_p((t)). This residue field is not perfect: t has valuation 1 and cannot be a p-th power, whose t-valuation would be divisible by p.

Passing to a perfect closure would introduce a new base and a new descent/comparison obligation; it is not a checked application to the saved family. Specializing t to a p-adic value could produce a separate one-parameter arithmetic curve, but would lose the free formal t parameter and the required relative connection/normalization interface. Pointwise applicability is not LC for the entire stated formal family.

Therefore the exact direct import
“Hyodo–Kato Theorem 5.1 directly proves LC over Z_p[[t]]”
is NOT_APPLICABLE.

This does not falsify LC, and does not say that no standard relative theorem can prove it. It blocks one precise, common shortcut using a theorem whose actual hypotheses are now pinned.

## Narrower interfaces in the same primary source

The same paper has genuinely more general relative material; it must not be hidden by the preceding negative result.

- Proposition 2.20, printed p. 238, computes log-crystalline cohomology of a crystal by the crystalline complex of an embedding system. The embedding definitions on pp. 236–238 and the PD/log-site conventions are part of its input. This is relevant to A, rather than itself a ready statement that the desired proper H^1 is a locally free nilpotent log F-module over the completed two-parameter base.
- Proposition 2.23, printed pp. 239–240, is a log-crystalline base-change statement under a smooth integral log morphism, a specified cartesian diagram, exact closed immersions/PD-subideals, a radicial base map and a flat crystal. Those conditions have not all been instantiated and composed with formal inverse limits here.
- Proposition 2.24, printed pp. 240–241, gives a relative Frobenius p-isogeny in projective systems for a smooth Cartier-type morphism over F_p, a compatible tower of flat Z/p^n thickenings with PD structures, and bounded logarithmic differential rank. It provides a promising precise ingredient for C after the target's log base/tower, Cartier type, theta base map and proper-cohomology passage are actually checked.

These are existing tools in the primary mathematical sense. Their statements are located, not silently promoted to a verified all-clauses LC theorem. In particular none of the displayed propositions alone is the normalization/dual-graph Frobenius identification D used to fix the sign.

A possible future import proof should explicitly instantiate the finite-level relative tower, prove the required cohomology/base-change and formal completion passages, and supply a normalization-compatible graph statement in the same convention. No such composite verification is claimed by this bounded unit.

## Stop condition and retained status

The assigned stop condition was to inspect at most three discriminating sources/theorem matches and stop when one import interface is established or refuted. The direct Theorem 5.1 match is conclusively rejected on its actual base hypothesis after one primary source. I therefore stop expanding the literature search.

Retain:
- the geometry certificate and the implication LC => mu=+1;
- CONDITIONAL_PASS_WITH_LC_OPEN for the earlier geometry package;
- actual c, extension xi/eta, integral/dagger/global full-carrier realization and the original functional as unresolved.

Do not mark actual regularity or the actual sign unconditionally proved. Do not label this as a proof that LC itself is false or impossible.

## OG15-LC-IMP-01 — Actual original theorem and direct base mismatch

Closed.

Original source: Hyodo–Kato, Astérisque 223 (1994), Exposé V, pp221–268, official PDF https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1994__223__221_0.pdf .

Theorem 5.1 on printed pp262–263 assumes a complete DVR A, mixed-characteristic fraction/residue fields, perfect characteristic-p residue field, canonical DVR log structure, proper log-smooth X and Cartier-type special log fibre. It compares the special-fibre log-crystalline inverse-limit object with generic-fibre de Rham cohomology after extending scalars to the trait's fraction field and choosing its uniformizer.

The fixed LC target instead concerns the relative formal family over Spf Z_p[[t]] with t=0 log divisor, theta(t)=t^p, identity coefficient Frobenius on its descent, formal/relative realization and normalization-compatible graph specialization. Z_p[[t]] is not a DVR: its maximal ideal (p,t) has two independent classes modulo its square. The required direct base hypothesis therefore fails, independently of the already checked semistable nodal geometry.

The canonical DVR log structure is also tied to the trait's closed point; it cannot simply be renamed as an arbitrary horizontal t-divisor on this two-parameter formal base. No formal-relative comparison follows directly from the title of the theorem.

## OG15-LC-IMP-02 — Attempted trait replacements and scope

Closed.

Q_p[[t]] is a complete DVR but has characteristic-zero residue field Q_p, so it does not meet the displayed characteristic-p residue hypothesis.

The p-adic completion of Z_p[[t]]_(p) has residue F_p((t)). This is imperfect because v_t(t)=1 while a p-th power has t-valuation divisible by p. Also t is invertible on that trait; its canonical closed-point log structure is the p-boundary, not the saved t=0 divisor. It therefore does not silently instantiate the same LC interface.

Perfecting the residue field or specializing t changes the input/base and leaves descent or relative reconstruction obligations. These failures prove NOT_APPLICABLE for the direct applications considered. They do not imply LC is false, impossible or absent from the wider literature.

The passage from Z_p[[t]][1/p] to Q_p[[t]] is itself a completion issue; these rings must not be silently equated. The fixed LC A-interface correctly retains that obligation.

## OG15-LC-IMP-03 — Located relative propositions and unfilled A–D bridge

Closed as a located-interface audit; mathematical realization remains open.

The report accurately distinguishes:
- Prop2.20, printed p238: embedding-system crystalline-complex realization with its log-PD/crystal inputs.
- Prop2.23, pp239–240: smooth-integral/cartesian/exact-PD base-change interface with flat crystal and the radicial map between the reduced bases in its diagram. “Radicial base map” must retain that exact diagram position.
- Prop2.24, pp240–241: smooth Cartier-type morphism in characteristic p, compatible flat finite-level PD tower, bounded log-differential rank and a relative-Frobenius p-isogeny of derived sheaf projective systems. The inverse-up-to-p^r statement is not an already constructed proper H1 module over the completed target base.

No proof presently binds these finite-level inputs to the exact formal family, passes all proper cohomology/base-change/completion steps, identifies the geometric generic source, and establishes the normalization/dual-graph/residue-kernel Frobenius convention. In particular D is not supplied merely by locating the relative Frobenius proposition.

Thus retain the previous CONDITIONAL_PASS_WITH_LC_OPEN geometry disposition and implication LC=>mu=+1. Actual geometric regularity/sign, c and extension constants, full-carrier integral/dagger/global realization and original functional obligations are not discharged.
